main_text.p: ius autem finis opus est: illius ve-rò veritas. Quamobrem Aristo-teles ibidem hoc philosophiæ ge-nus, quod omnino in contempla-tione rerum divinarum & cogni-tione versatur, scientiam veritatis nominat, nec iniuria, quadoquidem in vtraque theorica intelle-ctione veritas consistit. Alterum autem philosophiæ genus, quod in virtutis actione versatur, tresin partes distribui solet, quarum v-na recte honesteque viuendi via rationemque tradit, bonosque mores sequendi, & prauos declì-nandi iubet, atque præscribit: quā obrem ἠθικὴ[?] scientia dicitur. Alia est, quæ in rei familiaris admini-stratione versatur, ac proinde οἰκο-νομικὴ[?] nominatur. Alia denique est quæ regendorum regnorum ci-

page.notes: The first word "ius" is a fragment continuing from the previous page. The printed "ve-rò" is hyphenated across the line end. The Greek word "ἠθικὴ" after "obrem" is small and only partly legible, so it is marked [?]. The Greek "νομικὴ" after the hyphen "οἰκο-" is also doubtful, so it is marked [?]. The line ending "ci-" is continued on the next page. The two asterisks "**" below the text are printer's marks and were not transcribed. The faint word at the lower left ("Solid" or similar) is show-through and was left out.
